summary: Kemper County, MS tower: 1937 International Derrick model, NHLR-registered 2022 as US 1627; administered by the Mississippi Forestry Commission; no staffing or fire history found.

facts.design: 1937 International Derrick model with window shades, a 5-over-3 window layout and an opening six-pane section at the upper center
facts.status_note: The register page gives no visit date or current photo, so the standing status in our record is not confirmed by a dated source

visit.trail_note: Register says the site was heavily wooded and access to the base was next to impossible (visit date not given)

events.note: Register 'Built' field says around 1937; the description calls it a 1937 model International Derrick

evidence.supports: 1937 International Derrick model with window shades, 5-over-3 layout and opening six-pane section
evidence.quote: It's a 1937 model International Derrick, with the shades over the windows, and the 5 over 3 window configuration, with the upper center 6 pane section opening.

evidence.supports: International Derrick towers are rare where Aermotor towers are typical; the register's only narrative, with no staffing or fire history on the page
evidence.quote: This is rare International Derrick in a region that typically contains Aermotor towers.

evidence.supports: site heavily wooded and base hard to reach
evidence.quote: The site was heavily wooded and access to the base was next to impossible.

evidence.supports: administered by the Mississippi Forestry Commission
OpenStreetMap tags the structure as a lattice tower
OpenStreetMap tags the tower type as observation

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 373 ft (114 m), which matches the record's 113.7 m and is kept; OpenStreetMap's 118 m is not used

notes_for_editor: Only two sources were usable: the NHLR register page and the OSM node. Two web searches found no staffing, fire or current-status information. A WTOK headline from Aug 2026 about an alleged 'Porterville fire' in Kemper County does not mention the tower in the text we could read, so it is not used. Access and visit date are unknown; the register's access remark is recorded as a trail note only. The standing status is kept from the record but not dated by any source.
